summary: Fixed over-aggressive multi-channel decimation that left correlated EEG traces as long straight joins during timebase changes.

intervals.description: Inspect the attached EEG timebase recording, quantify sparse point selection for correlated channels, add adaptive extrema binning, and verify native timebase transitions.
evidence: User-provided recording Registrazione 2026-11-05 155756.mp4, decoded locally with VLC scene snapshots
Correlated 32-channel 9 Hz case before fix: 91 of 1500 points, maximum sample gap 0.5 s
Correlated 32-channel 9 Hz case after fix: 1090 points, maximum sample gap 0.0508 s
34 focused unit and GUI regression tests passed
Native Windows/OpenGL validator passed 30 renderer/channel/timebase transitions and 21 alternating 5 s/300 s checks with no errors

results: The video shows EEG becoming sparsely connected during window changes. The committed bin estimate divided the point budget by channel count, assuming per-channel extrema had unique timestamps. Correlated channels often share extrema, so the selected timestamp union could be far below budget and produce multi-cycle straight joins.

Raw preparation now begins with a finer source-time grid and reduces it only when the actual union of retained extrema exceeds the point budget. This common preparation path covers all raw modalities and renderer backends.
Added a correlated 32-channel EEG regression that checks both retained sample density and the point budget. Focused suites and native Windows/OpenGL transition and memory validation passed.
limitations: The numerical regression uses a deterministic correlated EEG-like signal. No commit or push was made; existing local modifications were preserved.
